title: Mirror top-k expert
hypothesis: A top-1 router over four logical expert views of one shared matrix can recover a four-expert teacher whose experts are shared-base Givens views, at lower actual model bytes than standard top-1 MoE; independent expert functions should require private residuals or full weights.
physical_object: one shared linear expert matrix W for a 16D-to-12D expert function
mirror_coordinate: per-logical-expert Givens coordinates on the hidden representation
logical_multiplicity: four router-addressable logical experts from one shared matrix
teacher: role is determined by signs of two input coordinates; aligned mode uses one shared base matrix plus four Givens views; independent mode uses four unrelated expert matrices

task.metric: held-out routed regression MSE and router role accuracy

controls: full MoE with rank-2 factorized router
shared expert plus scalar role gates
shared expert plus rank-1 per-role residual
shared expert plus Mirror Givens views

development.selection_metric: mean held-out routed MSE across methods and teacher modes

storage.authority: actual serialized full inference payload bytes
storage.serialization: torch.save state_dict plus deterministic config JSON

success_gate: In all three fresh aligned worlds, Mirror routed MSE <=1.10x standard full MoE, role accuracy >=99%, and actual full-model payload <=0.65x full MoE; it must beat hard tying and same-byte simple controls. Independent mode maps private-parameter boundary.
failure_gate: Mirror misses two or more aligned fresh quality gates, or rank-1/full-MoE control matches its quality with equal or lower payload. Independent-mode failure alone is a structural boundary, not overall failure.
boundaries: linear experts and synthetic router regions only
fixed 1,200-update screen, not capacity or natural-language claim

protocol_amendments.reason: Initial dev routed MSE was close to full MoE, but router role accuracy was 97.5-98.6%, below the registered 99% threshold; CE weight 0.2 left avoidable router errors on a deterministic four-quadrant label.
protocol_amendments.change: Increase auxiliary router CE weight from 0.2 to 1.0. Keep all methods, worlds, minibatches, learning rates, updates and quality gates unchanged. Preserve all dev_v1 rows; only v2 selects the LR and opens fresh worlds.

protocol_amendments.reason: With CE weight 1.0, dev_v2 router role accuracy remained around 98%, just below the 99% gate. The shared AdamW weight decay regularized router confidence along with the expert weights.
protocol_amendments.change: Use separate AdamW parameter groups: zero weight decay for router parameters, retain 1e-4 for expert/view parameters. Keep CE=1.0 and all other conditions unchanged. Preserve dev_v1/v2 rows; only v3 selects and may open fresh data.
